title: Scrum Framework
description: Scrum is an agile framework for managing complex projects, characterized by iterative progress and team self-organization. It emphasizes delivering working increments of a product while adapting to changing requirements.

roles.name: Scrum Master
responsibilities: Ensure the Scrum process is followed correctly

roles.name: Product Owner
responsibilities: Provide clear requirements and acceptance criteria
Has final authority on product features

roles.name: Development Team
responsibilities: Has autonomy in how to accomplish work

events.name: Sprint
key_points: No changes that endanger sprint goal

events.name: Daily Scrum
events.purpose: Synchronize activities and create a plan for the next 24 hours
notes: For the Development Team only (others may attend but not participate)
Held at the same time and place each day

events.name: Sprint Review
notes: Collaborative discussion about what was done
Informal meeting, not a status report

events.name: Sprint Retrospective
notes: Identifies what went well and what could be improved
Produces a concrete action plan for the next sprint

artifacts.name: Product Backlog
artifacts.description: Ordered list of everything needed in the product

artifacts.name: Sprint Backlog
artifacts.description: Selected items for sprint plus delivery plan
notes: Visible, real-time picture of the work planned

artifacts.name: Increment
artifacts.description: Sum of completed items during sprint

key_concepts.description: Regular check on progress and artifacts
How Scrum compares to other ways of organizing delivery work.

rows: Fixed-length iterations, prescribed roles and events
Kanban: continuous flow, fewer prescribed roles, limited WIP
Waterfall: sequential phases, complete specification upfront
XP: engineering practices (TDD, pair programming, continuous integration)

key_concepts.description: Frameworks used to apply Scrum across multiple teams working on one product.

backlog_management: INVEST criteria for stories (Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable)
sprint_execution: Maintain focus on the sprint goal
interview_tips: Emphasize practical experience over theoretical knowledge
Be prepared to describe how you've implemented Scrum in real projects
Discuss challenges you've faced with Scrum implementation and how you addressed them
Understand the difference between "doing Agile" and "being Agile"
Be honest about what worked and what didn't in your experience

common_pitfalls: Treating Scrum as a rigid process
Micromanagement by the Scrum Master or managers

metrics.name: Velocity
metrics.description: Amount of work completed per sprint
notes: Used for planning and capacity forecasting
Should be used as a team metric, not an individual one

metrics.name: Burndown Chart
notes: Shows progress toward the sprint goal

metrics.name: Sprint Goal Achievement
metrics.description: Success rate in meeting sprint goals
notes: Measures the team's ability to deliver on commitments

metrics.name: Lead/Cycle Time
metrics.description: Time taken from task creation to completion

metrics.name: Team Happiness
notes: Indicates whether the current pace is sustainable
